question.problem: Find the $y$-coordinate of the point on the curve $y={x}^{2}-2x$ that is closest to the point $(1,4).$
question.worked_solution:
Let us consider the *squared* distance $S$ between $(1,4)$ and a general point $P(x,y)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =(x-1)^{2}+(y-4)^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}-2x+1+{y}^{2}-8y+16 \\  & ={x}^{2}-2x+{y}^{2}-8y+17\end{aligned}
$$

We require that the point $P$ lies on the curve $y={x}^{2}-2x.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}S(y) & =y+{y}^{2}-8y+17 \\  & ={y}^{2}-7y+17.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the minimum distance, we take the first derivative of $S(y)$ and equate it to zero. This gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(y)=2y-7 & =0 \\ 2y & =7 \\ y & =\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that ${S}^{″}(y)=2>0.$ Therefore, $y=\frac{7}{2}$ is a minimum of $S.$

So, the squared distance (and therefore the actual distance) is minimized when $y=\frac{7}{2}.$
